item.title: Leah Litman, Lawless: How the Supreme Court Runs on Conservative Grievance, Fringe Theories, and Bad Vibes (Simon & Schuster, 2025) - The Burton Book Review
item.description: Leah Litman’s Lawless is an irreverent yet sobering account of the current Court’s willingness to further the Republican party’s most conservative agenda. Litman, a University of Michigan law professor and former clerk to Justice Kennedy, is well-known as a co-host of Strict Scrutiny, a podcast about the Supreme Court. item.title: Elon Musk defrauded Twitter investors in $44B buyout, jury finds
item.description: Technology billionaire and Tesla CEO Elon Musk committed securities fraud with false or misleading statements about Twitter’s fake bot accounts as he attempted to scrap or renegotiate the $44 billion deal to buy the social media platform, a California jury for a civil trial unanimously found Friday.

item.title: 2 lawyers convicted in staged truck accidents scheme
item.description: Two personal injury lawyers have been convicted by a federal jury in New Orleans for participating in a scheme to stage collisions with tractor-trailer trucks to collect large settlement payouts.

item.title: Goldman Sachs
item.description: The top lawyer at the Goldman Sachs Group Inc., who has been linked to disgraced multimillionaire financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, secured a $25 million pay package and new security perks in 2025 before she announced her upcoming resignation in June.

item.title: Google
item.description: Relatives of a Florida man who died by suicide after planning an act of “mass casualty” at the Miami International Airport are suing Google, alleging that its Gemini artificial intelligence chatbot escalated persuasive dialogue that caused the tragedy.

item.description: Musicians who argue that artificial intelligence companies have used their songs without permission are bringing litigation under a unique law in Illinois.

item.title: Legalweek 2026: Home bases, agentic AI and the race to own the lawyer’s desktop
item.description: Change is never easy, whether it’s transitioning your firm to generative artificial intelligence tools or acclimating to a new location for one of your favorite legal technology conferences. I was faced with the latter challenge earlier this month, when Legalweek, long hosted at the Midtown Hilton in New York City, moved to the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center on the western edge of Manhattan.

item.title: Highlights from the Legalweek
item.description: Ari Kaplan, a legal industry analyst and the host of the Reinventing Professionals podcast, recently spoke with attendees at the 2026 Legalweek conference about current trends and opportunities in the legal sector for his annual mixtape.
